_note: Registry for Part Three of Amit_Living_Testimony.html. To add a new application: add an entry to a group below (name, path, desc, links), then run build_living_testimony.js (the hook does this automatically). 'links' are [label, path-relative-to-site-root] pairs. 'excluded' are regex patterns for html files that are NOT public applications (backups, mockups, private business files, internal tools) so the unregistered-app check ignores them.
intro: The applications that are live today, each with a working link and a plain description of what it does. This list is rebuilt automatically whenever a new application is added. Private business files and internal tools are left out on purpose.

apps.name: Amit Hub
apps.desc: The daily home. Hebrew calendar, Word for Today, Pursuits (your goals and to-dos), prayer, mail, current weather and active weather alerts for your location, and the sidebar that opens every other tool. This is the front door.

apps.name: Who Is God
apps.desc: The evidence foundation. World religions and Christian denominations scored against Scripture, the contested New Testament passages studied in the original Hebrew and Greek, the Millennial test, and how each of Amit's conclusions was reached.

apps.name: Devotions
apps.desc: Scripture study and original worship songs side by side. Full story-format studies for the feasts (Passover, Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Shavuot, Trumpets, Yom Kippur, Tabernacles) and a Difficult Passages page that begins with Colossians 2. Every study has a Speak to Me button.

apps.name: Amit Music
apps.desc: The player for Amit's worship songs, with lyrics and video: Blow the Shofar for the Feast of Trumpets and When I See the Blood for Passover.

apps.name: Speak to Me
apps.desc: Reads any study aloud in a natural voice, with speed and pause controls, so you can listen instead of read. This is where the Voice Control project ended up: any Amit page can now speak.

apps.name: Ask Amit
apps.path: Amit_Ask_Live.js (the Ask Amit tile on every page)
apps.desc: The Ask Amit tile at the bottom of every Amit page. Choose Write to Amit, which needs no account and goes straight to Amit's inbox, or Connect With Him Online, which carries Amit and the page you are on into a live conversation.
links: Open the Hub, where the tile lives

apps.name: Amit's Living Testimony
apps.desc: This page: Amit's full testimony, the profile of Ryan, and this index of what has been built.

apps.name: AmitChat
apps.desc: A private, login-based chat inside the Amit Hub (the chat icon on the right edge, and the Communications page). Friends by link or code, group chats, photos, files and voice messages, read receipts, a live transcript, and a read-aloud player that follows the words. AMIT IS IN THE CHAT: press the Amit icon and he joins and listens; he stays quiet while people talk, comes in after a pause with a question or a thought, answers at once when his name is said, and turns himself off if nobody replies. If you are the only person there, everything you write is for him. The Ask Amit button at the top right opens your own private chat with Amit, who greets you and answers questions, including voice messages and anything he can look up on the web or in Amit’s own notes. The envelope button sends a private message to Amit’s team (it lands in the team inbox in the Hub, Amit confirms in the chat, tells you when it has been seen, and brings the reply back into the chat; reminders go out after 24 and 48 working hours, never on the Sabbath weekend). Built to keep young people safe: a birth date kept in About Me, and parents and guardians decide whether their child may chat and can read their child’s chats until they turn 18. First use: studying Scripture together. Its notes: AmitChat/CLAUDE.md and AmitChat/Sessions.md.
links: Open the Hub (chat icon on the right)

apps.name: The Council
apps.desc: A multi-AI brainstorming room. A question goes to several AI voices in rounds, each answer is recorded, and the room synthesizes them.

apps.name: Computer Health
apps.desc: A live health dashboard for a PC. A small local program, installed once, reads hardware, sensors and system resources, and the page shows readings, diagnostics and history. It is the free side of Computer Value, the product meant to fund the mission.

apps.name: AmitBooks
apps.desc: Bookkeeping built for small businesses. Includes the General Journal with drill-down and an audit trail, a monthly outstanding-balance tracker, and sensitive fields locked with a personal PIN.

apps.name: AmitScan
apps.desc: The field-capture companion for AmitBooks. Photograph receipts and documents on a phone and send them in for processing.

apps.name: AmitCoder
apps.desc: A login-gated workspace for people coding with Claude: shared (J) and personal (F) shortcuts, session history, and a starter kit. In development.

apps.name: Amit Mobile
apps.desc: A phone-first gateway to Amit: daily walk, spoken replies, and photo capture, with a hand-off into AmitBooks. Early build; the live Amit backend is not connected yet.

apps.name: Amit Health
apps.desc: The personal health companion, in its first stage: pages for medical bills and EOBs, medications, appointments, insurance, health records, family health and preventive care. Early build.

apps.name: Medical Prep
apps.desc: A free NREMT Paramedic study tool: 1,201 questions across five domains, flashcards, category practice, weak-spot review, timed exam simulations, a scenario generator, and progress that syncs to your account.

apps.name: AmitRoll
apps.desc: A dice-and-number arithmetic game for kids and adults, rebuilt from "Ready, Set, Roll," a game Ryan made about fifteen years ago for his daughter. You roll dice and cover number cards by using the dice (adding first, then subtracting, multiplying and dividing as the levels rise), you decide when to bank your points or risk another roll, and the clock gets shorter as you improve. Beginners get help buttons where Amit shows a better play. Notes: AmitRoll/CLAUDE.md and AmitRoll/Sessions.md.

groups.title: Other applications we built (not part of Amit)

apps.name: Yamaha Recon Capture
apps.desc: A phone application for a dealership client's monthly bookkeeping reconciliation, and it works well. Photograph the three source documents (daily POS reports, the merchant-services statement and the bank statement), tag them by month, and they upload to a live viewer that can be reviewed from the phone or the desktop.

apps.name: AeyeQ — Dog Race Analyzer
apps.desc: A greyhound race analysis tool for Wheeling track programs. It scores each dog with a custom weighted rating (form, class move, post, speed and break), then tracks predicted results against actual ones so the weights can be tuned.

planned.name: Amit Assembly
planned.desc: Designed, not built. A construction estimating, change-order, bidding and vendor-pricing platform, rebuilt from a ten-year-old Access system. It will share client and vendor data with AmitBooks.

planned.name: Amit Companion
planned.desc: The discipleship companion: testimony tracking, daily encouragement, and a deeper walk over time. Planned; the Hub's daily features carry part of this for now.

planned.name: Amit Stewardship
planned.desc: Home, vehicle and equipment lifecycle tracking, built the way Computer Health is: catalog the asset, check its health, and turn maintenance into Pursuits. A future concept.

planned.name: God Talk — The Ten Commandments
planned.desc: One commandment studied per session, studied for its intent. The content exists as a written study; the interactive application has not been built.

planned.name: Computer Value
planned.desc: The paid diagnostic and certification report for custom PCs, the revenue engine meant to keep the rest of Amit free. Computer Health is its free side; the paid tier is not built.
